nodes.summary: For a natural number $x$ let $K = \lfloor \exp(0.8 \sqrt{\log x}) \rfloor$ and, for a prime $p$, let $D_p = 1 + \lfloor \log x / \log p \rfloor$. Write $v_p(n)$ for the exponent of $p$ in a positive integer $n$. Then the number of integers $m$ with $1 \le m \le x$ for which some prime $p < 2K$ satisfies $\max \{ v_p(m + i) : 1 \le i \le K \} > D_p / \log D_p$ is $o(x)$ as $x \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Large valuations in short runs of consecutive integers are rare

nodes.summary: For a natural number $x$ let $K = \lfloor \exp(0.8 \sqrt{\log x}) \rfloor$ and, for a prime $p$, let $D_p = 1 + \lfloor \log x / \log p \rfloor$. Write $v_p(n)$ for the exponent of $p$ in a positive integer $n$. Then the number of integers $m$ with $1 \le m \le x$ for which some prime $p \le 2K$ satisfies $v_p\bigl(\binom{2m}{m}\bigr) \le D_p / \log D_p$ is $o(x)$ as $x \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Small valuations of the middle binomial coefficient are rare

nodes.summary: The set of natural numbers $m$ such that $\binom{m+k}{k}$ divides $\binom{2m}{m}$ for every integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le \exp(0.8 \sqrt{\log m})$ has natural density $1$.
nodes.title: Binomial coefficients dividing the middle binomial coefficient

nodes.summary: Write $v_p(n)$ for the exponent of a prime $p$ in a positive integer $n$, and for $m \ge 2$ let $\alpha_p(m) = v_p\bigl(\binom{2m}{m}\bigr) / (\log m / \log p)$. There is a set $S$ of natural numbers of natural density $1$ such that: $\alpha_2(m) \to 1/2$ as $m \to \infty$ within $S$; for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $\alpha_3(m) \ge 34/81 - \varepsilon$ for all sufficiently large $m \in S$; and $\alpha_p(m) \ge 0.39$…
nodes.title: Valuations of the middle binomial coefficient on a set of density one

nodes.summary: Let $\eta$ be a real number with $\eta < 1 / \log 4$. The set of natural numbers $m$ such that $(m+k)!/m! = (m+1)(m+2) \cdots (m+k)$ divides $\binom{2m}{m}$ for every integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le \eta \log m$ has natural density $1$.
nodes.title: Products of consecutive integers dividing the middle binomial coefficient

nodes.summary: Write $v_p(n)$ for the exponent of a prime $p$ in a positive integer $n$. The set of natural numbers $m$ such that $\max \{ v_p(m + i) : 1 \le i \le k \} \le 3 \log k / \log p$ for every integer $k$ with $\frac{1}{2} \log m < k < \log m$ and every prime $p \le 2k$ has natural density $1$.
nodes.title: Short runs of consecutive integers have small valuations almost always

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $k$ be natural numbers and $p$ a prime, and write $v_p(n)$ for the exponent of $p$ in a positive integer $n$. Then $v_p\bigl((m+k)!/m!\bigr) \le v_p(k!) + \max \{ v_p(m + i) : 1 \le i \le k \}$, where the maximum is $0$ when $k = 0$.
nodes.title: Valuation of a product of consecutive integers
